### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e485645f5f61f272e297a818ff62368bdd22d62a` — the merge of head `47907244a8aff8759707d796dd46cff55562c056` into base `fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e485645f5f61f272e297a818ff62368bdd22d62a && git checkout e485645f5f61f272e297a818ff62368bdd22d62a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23 47907244a8aff8759707d796dd46cff55562c056 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23 && git merge --no-ff 47907244a8aff8759707d796dd46cff55562c056

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `47907244a8aff8759707d796dd46cff55562c056`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.row-binding-column.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/package.json, packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-collection-fold.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/collection-item-owner-stamp.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, .changeset/28594-stored-connector-file-ref.md (on `main`)

Face: narrowing (`record-recognisers --paths` on the five changed paths decides no face and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `(narrowing)`; no `hits`). Floor: every path of the diff outside the two prose faces (`.changeset/28673-every-read-row-column-binding.md`, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, generated). Inputs: card #28673 (body, triage `6558366252`, claim `6558518628`, os-dev-report `6560371178`), PR #28734 (body, file list, `git diff 15e83114..47907244`), and the 48 check-runs on the head: 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending (`Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` 1-8/8, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Type Check UI` among them). Card premise holds: `15e83114` is #28671's squash merge, and the diff builds on its inline rule.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`withRowBinding` (protocol.ts 2672) changes meaning — right.** Base: stamp the column's package only while the body names none, return the body as it is otherwise. Head: the body's `_packageId` is never served; replaced by `boundPackageOf(column)` or deleted when that is `undefined`; same object returned only when the body already states the column's binding; copy otherwise. This is byte-for-byte the rule #28671 wrote inline in `storedOverlayEntries` (now a one-line call), so one spelling serves every site. The non-record guard moved ahead of `boundPackageOf`; non-records still pass through unchanged.
2. **Six read sites now state the column — right, and complete against the card's list.** Verified in the head tree: the list read (`protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts` 174), the by-name active read and the strict draft read (one site, 11398, `recPkg` = `record.package_id`), the by-name draft preview (11317, `recPkg` = `draftRec.package_id`), the draft list `placeDraft` (10248, column), the list merge (3149, `stored` records only), and the registry hydration `registerItem` line (18646, `options.packageId`, which the boot pull at 29166 and `getMetaItems` fill from the column) plus `hydrateExpandedViewItems` (19068). I scanned every `package_id ?? undefined|null` site in `protocol.ts` at the head: the remaining ones (11153 `serveDraft`'s verdict address, 22787 the migration report, 26679 `reboundFrom`) address a row and serve no body. No other module in the package stamps `_packageId` from a row (`meta-overlay-cache.ts` only mentions it in prose).
3. **The `#28409` override arms are preserved — right.** At 11312-11317 and 11389-11398 the `served.overrideOf` branch still serves the overridden package's `_packageId`, and `withRowBinding` runs only in the `else`. In the merge, `isServedOverrideRowOf` (served-override.ts) judges `row.package_id` and the body's `overrides.package`, never `_packageId`, so handing it a bound body changes no verdict; the slot still restamps `real` at 3193.
4. **The merge binds only `stored` contributions — right.** Every `stored`-bearing caller passes the row's column as `packageId`: `placed` and `overrideStandIns` use `storedOverlayEntries`' `recPkg`; `standIns` pass `undefined` for rows filtered to `package_id === null`; `placeDraft` passes the column. The MetadataService merge (10356) and `protocol-stored-collection-fold.ts` (137) pass no `stored`, so their records enter as before. No scope is ever stamped onto a package-less row.
5. **The two slot-stamp lines keep their spelling (3194, 10108) — right.** They state a SLOT's package for a stand-in, and their inputs are now bound at the source (every stored contribution, every `held` output of an earlier merge). With `withRowBinding` they would also run `boundPackageOf` over a slot key, which drops the `'sys_metadata'` sentinel. A foreign body stamp can no longer reach `chosen._packageId` from a stored row.
6. **View-container expansions — right.** `runtimeViewContainerPackage` (18748 region) reads `container._packageId` BEFORE `options.packageId`, which is precisely how a package-less container's body stamp placed its expansions in that package at the base. Binding the container to its column first makes the two agree; for a bound row with no stamp the outcome is identical to before.
7. **List read and `'sys_metadata'` — right, with an observation.** `storedOverlayEntries` now drops a column reading the sentinel (via `boundPackageOf`) where #28671's inline rule served it. The hydrator has always normalised so; no writer stores the sentinel; and in `getMetaItems` the merge restamps it from the contribution's `pkg` at 3194, so the list's served item is unchanged. Direct readers of the entries (the connector materializer) see none, which is what every sentinel reader already reads it as. Not a finding.
8. **Public surface — unchanged, right.** `withRowBinding` is `export`ed from `protocol.ts` for its sibling module only; `package.json` `exports` is `.` alone and `index.ts` has no `export *` and does not name it. `check:api-surface` sits in the green Lint gates.
9. **Accept-set — no change.** No door, no schema, no `packages/spec` hunk, no gate. The save door (`stripDerivedProvenance`, `DERIVED_PROVENANCE_KEYS` at 2593) and the registration judge are untouched.
10. **Tests — right shape.** 21 cases cover the rule and each of the six sites with a control each, red on #28671's head and green at this head per the report; the ablation on the by-name site reds exactly its three pins. Judged on the head's `Test Core` runs, which are green.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28673-every-read-row-column-binding.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` — **correct.** Line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset body; title carries `!`; BREAKING banner present with Before / Now / Unchanged / Who-sees-it; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `Check Changeset` and the Lint gates (which hold `check:adr-0087-registration`) are green on the head.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is right.** What an author can write is unchanged: a body `_packageId` has been stripped at the save door since #16702 and refused at the registration door by the ADR-0010 judge, so no key is added, removed, refused or re-meant. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task §3, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition — which this does.
- **The `(narrowing)` arm is right** (answers the dev's open question — see ③). The served `_packageId` of a stored row whose body carries a foreign stamp shrinks to the column's at every read; readers that take an item's owner from it (the disabled-package filter, artifact scoping, the security catalog) observe a different owner for such rows. That is the same arm #28671's changeset declared for the same rule at the list read, and the two changesets read alike. Clause-②: `no (narrowing)`, not widened anywhere.
- No `skip-changeset`; the diff ships from a released package.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (Clause-② arm, A vs B): A, keep `no (narrowing)`.** Rationale in ②. No regrade; nothing for the dev to change.
- **Out-of-scope 1 (noted, not filed): `stored-row-binding.ts` header in PR #28693.** Not on `main`, not an input here; the sentence "`withRowBinding` keeps a body's own stamp" becomes false once both land. Escalated to the lane seat as a one-line correction owed by whichever PR lands second; `boundPackageOf` vs `bindStoredRow` on the sentinel is #28693's own question. No action on this PR.
- **Out-of-scope 2 (noted, not filed): PR body says "61 commands" where the final head derived 69.** Prose of the dispatching seat's own body, not reviewed here; the gate verdicts are read off the check-runs, which are green.
- **Dev's acceptance notes** (slot-stamp lines kept, sentinel at the list read, #28693 coexistence): each verified in ① items 5, 7 and 3 — none is a flag left standing.
- No dev flag is unanswered; nothing further to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against the published spec on `main`: ADR-0010 as stated in `packages/spec/src/kernel/collection-item-owner-stamp.ts` ("`_packageId` is the ADR-0010 envelope stamp: the package that REGISTERS the item … A body never names its own owner, so the stamp is refused, with a prescription") and `protocol.zod.ts` (`packageId`: "Owning package machine id"). The save door has stripped `_packageId` from every stored body since #16702 (`DERIVED_PROVENANCE_KEYS`). So the spec declares no capability for an author to bind a stored row to a package through its body, and the only writer of a row's package is its `package_id` column. A body stamp the read echoed was a value the spec already refused at both doors; serving the column instead **makes the spec's own refusal real at the read** and takes nothing declared away from any consumer. Not an implementation gap narrowed at the consumer: the capability (a row bound to a package) is delivered, by the column, at every read.

Break attempts, each held:
- A declared override row (`#28409`) is bound to the pair's column but served as the base package's: the `overrideOf` arms run first at both by-name sites and the merge restamps `real` — verified, unchanged.
- A scope passed as `packageId` to the merge could stamp a package-less row: no `stored` caller passes one (① item 4).
- A view container's expansions could move for a bound row: `runtimeViewContainerPackage` already preferred the body stamp, so binding the body first only closes the echo (① item 6).
- A cached row's body could be written: `withRowBinding` copies whenever it changes anything; the `_draft = true` mutations at 10269 and 11318 land on a fresh `convertStoredItem` result or a copy.
- `transform(bound, prev)` in the active list merge: the view-identity healing at 9958 reads no `_packageId`.

Findings:
- **S1 (should-fix): stale header prose in the touched file.** `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry`'s `## [#23233]` section (protocol.ts ~18492-18497) still says "a body that already names a `_packageId` keeps it" and "The expansions of a view container are registered from the unstamped row, as before". Both sentences are false at this head: the stamp is replaced or dropped, and the container is expanded under its column binding (19068). The `withRowBinding` docblock and the two call-site comments say the new rule; the module header should too. One-paragraph edit, no behaviour.
- No must-fix.
